chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who misses the witr during the night. He said: He should make it up as witr whenever he remembers, even if the sun has passed the meridian.

And the second explanation regarding the previous reports is that it is directed toward one who is negligent regarding salat and deliberately abandons it, by way of sternness against him; that indicates this.

key_terms.التَّغْلِيظِ: speaking with severity or stern emphasis
key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the witr prayer performed in the night prayer cycle
key_terms.تَرْكَهَا: abandoning it, referring to the prayer
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian, meaning after noon
key_terms.يَتَهَاوَنُ: he treats the matter lightly or negligently
key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: he makes it up as qaḍāʾ after missing it

ai.seo_question: When should a missed witr prayer be made up according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that one who misses the witr prayer at night should perform its qaḍāʾ as witr whenever he remembers, even after midday. It also notes that other reports can be understood as applying stern language to one who deliberately neglects salat, indicating a distinction between forgetfulness and intentional abandonment.
